context:
Goal: keep the global CLAUDE.md small, with each rule loading where it must act.
Problem (rule): the audit moves most of the Output section out of the global CLAUDE.md, and nothing moves without your sign-off.
Based on (ruling): your 12:38 and 12:40 CST Nov 11 words on moving sections, "it would need my sign off".
Based on (measured): the plan's word counts, and its load test: a rule that stops an act must load before that act.
Departs from: main — "Write plainly" (11 words) moves to the output style, and the owner-question rules (about 230 words) move to skill waiting-page (this page's rules), leaving a one-line stop rule global.
Meanwhile: nothing moves before your answer; the guard test file split this waited on is done (merged 07:16 CST Nov 12).
Re-checked 11:39 CST Nov 12: the quoted text is unchanged on the shared main branch. Correction: "Write plainly" also governs text Claude writes for its own agents (briefs and reports), and the reply style named shiv-stylisms covers only replies to you, so moving it there leaves agent text with no plain-writing rule. Whether that style loads in agents is unmeasured.

options.gain: About 230 words leave the global file.
options.how: The lane moves the text as the plan proposes.
options.label: Accept the split
options.lose: The question rules load only when skill waiting-page fires; if it misses, a session may open a question box while agents run.

options.gain: The rule loads in every session, before any act.
options.label: Keep it global
options.lose: No words leave the global file.

reply: Recorded 12:00 CST: the split is accepted. Sent to lane global-claude-md-scope-audit, with the re-check's note that agent text needs a plain-writing rule wherever Write plainly lands.
title: Where the Output section of CLAUDE.md lives
why: The lane's pick: most of the section acts only when a session has a question, which is when the skill fires.
